en: The Candra-sūtra.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Campā on the bank of the Gargarā lotus pond.
Now at that time, the entire lunar disk had been eclipsed by Rāhu, the lord of the asuras.

Then the deity who resided in that lunar disk—frightened, terrified, agitated, and with the hair on her body standing on end—approached the Blessed One. Having approached, she bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, she addressed the Blessed One in verse:
Homage to you, O Buddha, the hero who is completely liberated in every way;
I have entered into distress—be my refuge.
In this world, the Moon has gone for refuge to the Sugata, the Arhat;
O Rāhu, release the Moon! The Buddhas are compassionate toward the worlds.
The Blessed One replied with a verse:
"He who, like Vairocana, is the light-maker in the darkness of the sky..."
O Rāhu, do not swallow the moon in the mid-air;
release quickly this lamp of all creatures!
With his body perspiring, distressed and oppressed like a man in agony, Rāhu quickly released the lunar disc.
At that time, Bāḍi was an asura, the grandson of Virocana. Bāḍi, the grandson of Virocana, saw the lunar disk being released very hurriedly by Rāhu, the lord of the asuras;
and having seen it, at that moment he spoke this verse:
Why indeed do you, Rāhu, release the moon in such haste, with your limbs perspiring and trembling like a man who is oppressed and in distress?
Rāhu said: "My head shall split into seven pieces and I shall find no happiness while living, if I do not release the moon here as proclaimed by the Buddha."
Then Bāḍi, the grandson of Virocana, spoke in verse:
… the Fully Awakened Ones who see the truth …;
by the chanting of their verses, Rāhu releases the moon.
The Candra-sūtra is completed.
